title: Economic Fidelity Controller and Safeguards — design manual
author: Arjun Mehta
content:
Overview

This document specifies the Economic Fidelity Controller (EFC): a runtime subsystem that dynamically balances model fidelity, latency, and per-token cost across hosted and dedicated deployments. The EFC is a control plane component embedded in the serving stack that enforces cost and quality guardrails through real-time signals to the scheduler and kernel selection layer.

Goals
- Enforce organization-level cost targets (per-customer and aggregated) while preserving user-facing quality SLOs.
- Provide a transparent, auditable policy surface for degradations and fidelity regressions.
- Make runtime fidelity decisions reversible and safe: all changes must be observable, attributable, and subject to automatic rollback.
- Integrate with existing runtime scheduler and kernel mapper without adding undue tail-latency risk.

Scope and non-goals
- In-scope: model variant selection, dynamic quantization profiles, request routing to cheaper device pools, short-lived fidelity steps (e.g., sequence-length bucketing, KV cache hints), telemetry and alerting.
- Out of scope: training-time quantization decisions, model architecture changes, long-term contractual pricing.

High-level architecture

Components:
- runtime-efc (control loop service) — computes per-cohort fidelity actions every 5s by default.
- scheduler-proxy — receives EFC actions and converts them to scheduler admission rules / kernel hints.
- kernel-guard — lightweight in-node agent that applies kernel variant selection and enforces per-request fidelity caps.
- telemetry-bridge — aggregates fidelity decisions, token/cost deltas, and model quality signals for dashboards and audits.

Data flows (textual diagram)
1) telemetry -> runtime-efc: raw signals (per-route latency P50/P95/P99, per-token cost, embed/call counts, quality regressions from evals) flow to runtime-efc via the telemetry-bridge.
2) runtime-efc -> scheduler-proxy: actionable policy (e.g., reduce high-cost customer cohort fidelity to F-2 for 60s; route low-priority cohort to econ-gpu-pool).
3) scheduler-proxy -> kernel-guard: concrete kernel variant and admission instructions.
4) kernel-guard -> runtime (per request): tag request with fidelity metadata; enforce runtime caps.

Control loop semantics
- Decision cadence: default 5s decision window with exponential backoff on oscillation.
- Safety multiplier: every action carries a safety_multiplier (0.0–1.0); actions with multiplier < 0.25 require manual approval for tenant-broad changes.
- Confidence scoring: runtime-efc assigns confidence based on sample size and historical stability. Actions with confidence < 0.5 are restricted to shadow mode.

Policy primitives
- fidelity-step: an atomic change (e.g., quantize to int8, switch model variant to compact-v2, reduce max_tokens from 1024 -> 512).
- cohort-selector: matches requests to cohorts using route, customer_tier, token_budget, and tags.
- duration: TTL for the fidelity-step (e.g., 30s, 5m, 1h).
- escalation: if action persists > escalation_window, EFC escalates to an owner and can trigger rollback policies.

Telemetry and signals
Key signals (ingested via telemetry-bridge):
- latency_p50, latency_p95, latency_p99 (ms) per route and per cohort
- tokens_consumed and cost_per_token (USD) per model variant
- quality_score_{promptset} (0..1) from continuous evals and prompt-set checks
- kv_cache_hit_rate and sequence_length_distribution
- kernel_switch_rate and kernel_error_rate
- packing_efficiency and batch_size_distribution

SLOs and thresholds (examples)
| signal | target | warning | critical | owner |
|--------|--------|---------|----------|-------|
| route_latency_p95 | <= 450ms | > 550ms | > 800ms | runtime-sre |
| per_token_cost (30m window) | <= $0.0009 | > $0.0012 | > $0.0020 | finance-eng |
| quality_score_regression | delta <= -0.03 | delta <= -0.06 | delta <= -0.12 | applied-ml |

Integration with scheduler and kernels
- API handshake: runtime-efc exposes a gRPC action stream to scheduler-proxy: Action { cohort_id, fidelity_step, ttl_s, safety_multiplier, cause_id }
- Scheduler-proxy resolves conflicts between multiple controllers (e.g., operator-initiated vs EFC) by priority: manual > experiment > EFC > default.
- Kernel hinting: fidelity_step maps to kernel tags (e.g., quant-int8, split-attn-low, kv-prefetch-disabled). kernel-guard translates tags into in-node flags.

Kernel selection pseudocode (simplified)
1) request arrives with cohort_id
2) kernel_tag = kernel-guard.lookup(cohort_id) 
3) selected_kernel = kernel_catalog.best_match(kernel_tag, request.shape)
4) if selected_kernel.unavailable -> fallback to nearest-fidelity kernel and report metric efc.kernel_fallback

Example policies
- Cost cap policy: if per_token_cost (30m) for a customer > $0.0012 AND kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.3 -> apply fidelity-step: compact-v2 for 15m with safety_multiplier=0.6.
- Latency preservation: if route_latency_p95 degradation > +150ms -> temporarily reduce batching for the affected cohort and escalate to SRE.

Rollout checklist (canary-driven)
1) Merge feature branch to canary runtime-efc service (canary tag: efc-canary-202602).
2) Enable EFC in shadow mode for 48h on canary cluster; compare hypothetical actions to baseline.
3) Metric guard checks (must pass): no more than 0.5% increase in route_p99, no knock-on increase in kernel_error_rate.
4) Release to 5% of traffic by cohort and run for 2h. Verify cost deltas and quality-signal drift.
5) Expand to 25%/2d, 67%/24h, global after 72h if stable.

Operational runbook: fidelity-induced incident
(Owner: runtime-sre)
1) Detect: Alert fired for quality_score_regression critical or per_token_cost critical.
2) Triage: Check EFC action timeline (telemetry-bridge -> EFC decisions). Identify cohort_id and action_id.
3) Immediate mitigation: disable EFC (runtime-efc -> pause) for impacted tenant cohort or set safety_multiplier=0.0 to force rollback.
4) Containment: if kernel_error_rate correlated, instruct kernel-guard to revert to baseline kernel tag.
5) Root cause: run hypothesis list (network contention, quantization misestimate, eval false-positive). Use request traces (trace_id) and shadow logs.
6) Postmortem: produce PM with signal graphs (pre/post), action timeline, and an action to add new test prompts if regression was genuine.

Testing and benchmark plan
- Unit tests: decision engine determinism, hysteresis math, TTL expiry.
- Integration tests: runtime-efc -> scheduler-proxy gRPC mocking with fault injection.
- E2E perf: run mixed-workload tracer across three synthetic cohorts (chat-short, chat-long, embedding-heavy). Measure: per_token_cost, p99 latency, quality-score drift.
- Regression tests (daily): run a 1h mini-run against the baseline cluster using representative prompt-sets and assert quality_score >= baseline - 0.02.

Sample test matrix (human-readable)
| workload | mocked signal | expectation |
| chat-short (50k reqs) | spike in tokens_consumed | EFC recommends compact-v2 for low-priority cohort; no p99 increase > 5% |
| embedding-burst (10k reqs) | sudden cost uplift | EFC routes to econ-gpu-pool; verify latency change within 20% |

Auditing and compliance
- Every EFC action is logged as immutable event: {action_id, timestamp, cohort_id, pre_state_hash, post_state_hash, actor=efc, reason_code}. Events are retained 365 days in audit-store.
- For enterprise customers with private deployments, EFC can be configured in read-only (advisory) mode.

Dashboards and alerts (owner mappings)
- EFC Decisions dashboard: lists active fidelity-steps, safety_multiplier, and confidence scores (owner: runtime-ops).
- Cost drift dashboard: per-customer cost trends (owner: finance-eng).
- Fidelity regressions: quality-score delta alerts to applied-ml slack channel and paging for critical regressions.

Appendix: practical examples and CLI snippets
- Inspect active EFC actions (CLI):
  $ rctl efc list --cluster canary --format json | jq '.active_actions[] | {action_id, cohort, fidelity_step, ttl_s, safety_multiplier}'

- Simulate a cost cap policy (pseudo-YAML):
  policies:
    - id: cost-cap-01
      selector: {customer_tier: silver, route_tag: public-chat}
      condition: 'per_token_cost_30m > 0.0012 and kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.3'
      action: {fidelity_step: compact-v2, ttl_s: 900, safety_multiplier: 0.6}

- Example audit event (log line):
  2026-02-10T15:02:03Z efc.action CREATED action_id=ac_7b9f cohort=tenant-124 pre_hash=ha1 post_hash=ha2 reason=cost_cap_01

Glossary
- fidelity-step: concrete runtime change that reduces compute/precision to save cost.
- cohort: a request grouping key (route + customer_tier + tags).
- kernel-guard: in-node enforcement agent.
